tool.name: create_identity_finding
tool.description:
Create an identity security finding for the Entra ID audit report.
Use this tool to document a confirmed identity security issue discovered during the audit. Only call this AFTER you have validated the finding with evidence from the Graph API tools — do not report theoretical or unconfirmed issues.
finding_type values map to audit domains: - stale_identity → from entra_list_stale_users / entra_list_stale_service_principals - privileged_role → from entra_list_privileged_role_assignments - app_permission → from entra_list_app_permissions - guest_access → from entra_list_guests - ca_gap → from entra_list_conditional_access_policies - sod_conflict → from entra_list_role_assignments_per_user
DO NOT USE: - For theoretical or unconfirmed issues - When affected_objects is empty or unknown - To re-report an already reported finding (deduplication is enforced) - For general observations without a specific identity object

parameter.name: finding_type
parameter.description: Category of finding. Must be one of: stale_identity, privileged_role, app_permission, guest_access, ca_gap, sod_conflict

parameter.name: title
parameter.description: Short descriptive title identifying the specific finding. Examples: - "Stale Global Admin Account — jsmith@contoso.com" - "Guest User with Privileged Role — ext_vendor@gmail.com" - "MFA Not Enforced for All Users — Conditional Access Gap" - "SoD Conflict: User Administrator + Authentication Administrator — alice@contoso.com"

parameter.name: severity
parameter.description:
Severity level. Must be one of: critical, high, medium, low, informational
Guidance: - critical: Direct path to tenant takeover (e.g. stale Global Admin, SP with GA role) - high: Significant risk requiring prompt action (e.g. guest with privileged role, no MFA policy) - medium: Elevated risk with mitigating factors (e.g. stale account >90d, broad delegated grants) - low: Minor risk or policy violation (e.g. expired credential on low-privilege app) - informational: Observation without immediate risk

parameter.name: affected_objects
parameter.description: JSON string — list of Entra objects affected by this finding. Format: [{"object_id": "...", "display_name": "...", "object_type": "user|servicePrincipal|group|app"}] Must contain at least one object. Use exact object_id values from Graph API responses.

parameter.name: description
parameter.description: Clear explanation of what was discovered and how: - What the API returned (specific values, dates, counts) - Which tool was used to find it - Why the configuration is a security problem Be specific — reference the affected objects by name.

parameter.name: impact
parameter.description: Business and security impact if this finding is not remediated: - Who or what is at risk (users, data, tenant, third parties) - What an attacker could do if they exploit this gap - Potential compliance or regulatory implications Do NOT repeat the description — focus on consequences, not what was found.

parameter.name: evidence
parameter.description: JSON string — raw API response excerpts that confirm the finding. Include the key fields from the Graph API response that prove the issue (e.g. last_sign_in_datetime, role_name, permission_value, account_enabled). Do not include sensitive credential values.

parameter.name: remediation
parameter.description: Specific, actionable remediation steps for the tenant admin. Include Azure portal navigation paths or PowerShell/Graph API commands where applicable. Examples: - "Disable the account in Entra admin center > Users > [user] > Edit > Account status" - "Remove the Global Administrator role via PIM > Role assignments > [user] > Remove" - "Create a Conditional Access policy requiring MFA for all users under Security > Conditional Access"

parameter.name: risk_score
parameter.description: Override risk score between 1 and 10. If 0 or omitted, derived from severity: critical=9, high=7, medium=5, low=3, informational=1

parameter.name: tenant_id
parameter.description: Azure tenant ID (GUID). If omitted, inferred from AZURE_TENANT_ID environment variable.

returns.description: Response containing: - success: bool - message: Confirmation or error message - report_id: Generated finding ID (on success) - finding_type: Echo of input finding_type - severity: Echo of input severity - risk_score: Effective risk score used - errors: List of validation error messages (on failure) - duplicate_of: ID of the existing duplicate finding (if duplicate detected)

function.parameter: User jsmith@contoso.com holds the Global Administrator role but has not signed in for 247 days (last sign-in: 2025-08-03). Discovered via entra_list_stale_users with stale_threshold_days=90.

A dormant Global Administrator account is a high-value target. If the credentials are compromised — via phishing, credential stuffing, or a data breach — an attacker gains unrestricted tenant-wide control: creating backdoor accounts, exfiltrating all directory data, disabling security controls, and persisting access indefinitely with no detection signal from normal usage patterns.

1. Confirm with the account owner whether the account is still required. 2. If no longer needed: Entra admin center > Users > jsmith@contoso.com > Edit properties > Account status > Disabled. 3. Remove the Global Administrator role via Entra admin center > Roles and administrators > Global Administrator > Remove assignment. 4. If account is required, enforce re-authentication and review role necessity — consider replacing with a less-privileged role.
No Conditional Access Policy Enforcing MFA for All Users

No enabled Conditional Access policy requires MFA for all users across all applications. entra_list_conditional_access_policies returned 3 enabled policies and 1 report-only policy, none of which enforces MFA for all users or blocks legacy authentication.

Without MFA, any leaked or guessed password grants immediate, unrestricted access to all cloud applications. Password spray and credential stuffing attacks succeed at scale against tenants without MFA. This is the single highest-impact gap in identity security — Microsoft reports 99.9% of account compromise attacks are stopped by MFA.
{"enabled_policies": 3, "report_only_policies": 1, "gap_signals": ["No enabled policy enforces MFA for all users", "Legacy authentication protocols not blocked"]}

1. Navigate to Entra admin center > Security > Conditional Access > New policy. 2. Assign to: All users (exclude break-glass accounts). 3. Target: All cloud apps. 4. Grant: Require multi-factor authentication. 5. Enable the policy in enforcement mode (not report-only). 6. Also create a separate policy to block legacy authentication protocols.
